name: VisiBeacon – llms.txt, AI Crawler Tracking and AI Search Visibility
author: miotix

sections.description:
AI answer engines are the new search. VisiBeacon makes your WordPress site visible, readable and quotable for them – a practice known as Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).

Free features

  • llms.txt generator – serves a spec-compliant /llms.txt file (per llmstxt.org): site name, summary, and curated link sections with descriptions. Auto-updates as your content changes. Works alongside Yoast, Rank Math, SEOPress and AIOSEO (reuses their meta descriptions).
  • AI bot detection – see which AI crawlers visit your site: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, Meta, Amazon, Cohere, Mistral and more, with a 30-day “which AI engines see you” overview on the dashboard.
  • Per-bot crawler controls – allow, block via robots.txt, or hard-block (403) each AI bot individually. Block training bots while staying visible to AI search.
  • FAQ + FAQPage schema – add FAQ sections to any post or page with valid FAQPage JSON-LD and accordion styling, from a simple editor in the post sidebar.
  • Active AI push (IndexNow) – publishes and updates are pushed instantly to the index that powers ChatGPT search. No account needed.

VisiBeacon Pro (separate plugin, sold on visibeacon.com)

  • AI traffic trends – daily crawl charts, most-crawled URLs, recent activity and referral visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and other AI engines.
  • Readiness score – analyzes each post for what AI engines need: a direct answer near the top, question headings, scannable structure, FAQ, freshness. Graded A-D with a fix checklist.
  • Auto-generated FAQs – one-click FAQ generation per post (manual FAQ editing is free).
  • llms-full.txt – full-content companion file for deeper AI ingestion.
  • AI enhancement (optional) – bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API key for AI-written summaries, descriptions and FAQs.

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services. No service is required – each can be disabled in the plugin settings, and the plugin remains functional without them.

IndexNow (api.indexnow.org, operated by Microsoft Bing)
Purpose: the “Active AI push” feature submits the public URLs of your published content (and your llms.txt URL) to the IndexNow endpoint so search and AI engines index changes faster.
Data sent: your site’s host name, the public URLs being submitted, and a plugin-generated verification key. Sent when you publish or update content, and when you click “Push all URLs now”. No personal data, post content, or visitor data is sent.
Can be disabled: VisiBeacon → IndexNow → Active AI push.
Terms: https://www.indexnow.org/faq | Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

VisiBeacon bot registry (visibeacon.com)
Purpose: once a week the plugin downloads an updated list of known AI crawler user-agents from visibeacon.com/bots.json so new AI bots are detected without waiting for a plugin update.
Data sent: a standard HTTP GET request (your server’s IP and WordPress user-agent, as with any HTTP request). No site content or personal data is sent.
Terms: https://visibeacon.com/terms/ | Privacy: https://visibeacon.com/privacy-policy/

The AI traffic tracker stores its data locally in your own database only. Visitor IP addresses are stored as salted hashes by default and can be anonymized entirely. No analytics or tracking data is sent to any third party.

Third-party libraries

  • Chart.js v4 (https://www.chartjs.org) – MIT License – bundled unmodified at admin/js/vendor/chart.umd.min.js for the admin dashboard charts.
sections.faq:
What is llms.txt?

A proposed standard (llmstxt.org) that gives large language models a concise, curated map of your site – like robots.txt, but for helping AI understand and cite your content rather than just crawl it.

Does this plugin send my content to third parties?

No. The free plugin sends no post content anywhere. (The separate Pro plugin has an optional bring-your-own-key AI feature; even there, nothing is sent unless you add a key.)

Does it work with my SEO plugin?

Yes. VisiBeacon complements Yoast, Rank Math, SEOPress and AIOSEO – it reuses their meta descriptions in llms.txt and adds GEO features they don’t have.

Does uninstalling delete my data?

No. Your settings, AI traffic history, FAQs and readiness scores are kept when the plugin is deleted, so reinstalling picks up right where you left off. If you want a full cleanup instead, enable “Remove ALL VisiBeacon data when the plugin is deleted” on the “Data & Backup” tab before uninstalling. You can also export a complete JSON backup (and import it back) from the “Data & Backup” tab.

Will blocking AI bots hurt my rankings?

Blocking training-only bots (e.g. GPTBot) does not affect Google rankings. Blocking AI search bots (e.g. OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) will reduce your visibility in those AI engines – the plugin labels each bot’s purpose so you can decide.
sections.changelog:
1.9.7

  • Fixed: the free plugin shipped a native uninstall.php alongside the bundled licensing SDK. WordPress runs that file instead of the uninstall hook the SDK registers, so the SDK’s own uninstall flow never ran when the plugin was deleted. The data cleanup is now wired through the SDK’s uninstall hook, exactly like the Pro editions. No behavior change for your data: cleanup still runs on delete and still removes data only when “Remove ALL VisiBeacon data when the plugin is deleted” is enabled on the Data & Backup tab.

1.9.6

  • New: “Generate a new key” button on the IndexNow tab. IndexNow caches its verification verdict per domain and key, so a domain that failed verification while the key file was unreachable can keep answering HTTP 403 for weeks even after the file works. A fresh key carries no cached verdict – every domain is verified anew on the next push.
  • Fixed: on multilingual sites the llms.txt conflict notice could reappear even after VisiBeacon was correctly serving the file, wrongly naming an installed SEO plugin as the source. The check compared the live file (served in the site’s primary language) against the admin language’s version – it now recognizes VisiBeacon’s own output in any language.
  • Improved: when the serving source of /llms.txt cannot be identified from its content, the notice no longer names a plugin whose llms.txt feature is verifiably switched off.

1.9.5

  • Fixed: on multilingual sites, the Key pages and Excluded content pickers mixed every language’s items together (wp-admin does not filter queries by language, and WPML’s “All languages” admin mode never does). The pickers now list only the edited language’s items; items of untranslatable post types stay listed in every language, matching how the multilingual plugin serves them.
  • Fixed: the published counts next to Content sections (and the max-items overflow warning) counted every language’s items on multilingual sites. They now count the edited language’s items.

1.9.4

  • New: per-language llms.txt switch on multilingual sites – “Serve llms.txt for this language” on the llms.txt tab, set per language. Uncheck it for languages that are defined on the site but not really in use: that language’s llms.txt (and llms-full.txt) returns 404 and its link leaves the Dashboard list, while every other language keeps serving. Existing sites are unaffected – every language stays enabled until you switch it off.
  • New: “select all” checkbox on every content-type group in the Key pages and Excluded content pickers – one click selects or clears a whole type (Posts, Pages, Products…), with a dash state when only some items are picked.
  • New: FAQ status table on the FAQ tab – every published item with its FAQ count and a direct edit link, so you can see at a glance which pages still need questions. (Pro installs keep their richer table with generation buttons.)
  • Improved: the FAQ tab now says clearly where editing happens – each item’s questions live on the item itself, edited from the VisiBeacon box in its editor sidebar, and the tab’s Edit links take you straight there.
  • Improved: ticking a content type under “Content sections” now reveals that type’s items in the Key pages and Excluded content pickers immediately – no more saving first just to see them. Picks made for a type you later untick are also no longer silently dropped on the next save.
  • Improved: FAQ placement (append after content vs schema only) is now set per language on multilingual sites, like the FAQ heading. A language without its own choice follows the primary language, so existing sites behave exactly as before.

1.9.3

  • New: “Free vs Pro” tab – a plain comparison of what the free plugin includes (everything listed stays fully functional) and what the separate Pro plugin adds. Nothing in the free plugin is locked or disabled; the tab is purely informative and disappears when Pro is installed.
  • Improved: when an IndexNow push fails for some domains on a multi-domain site, only the failed domains’ URLs are kept for the automatic retry – the domains that went through count as pushed and are not re-sent. The verification error message now also explains that IndexNow re-checks key files periodically, so a 403 can persist for a while after the key file becomes reachable and then clears on its own.

Earlier releases are documented in changelog.txt, bundled with the plugin.

upgrade_notice.1.9.6: IndexNow: a new "Generate a new key" button unsticks domains that keep failing key verification (HTTP 403), plus fixes for false llms.txt conflict notices on multilingual sites.
upgrade_notice.1.9.4: Multilingual quality of life: per-language llms.txt switch, "select all" per content type, a FAQ status table, pickers that update as you tick content sections, and per-language FAQ placement.
upgrade_notice.1.9.2: Multilingual fix: every language's llms-full.txt now carries that language's own content, and the bulk tools' Stop button stops all languages.
upgrade_notice.1.9.1: IndexNow fix for servers that answer .txt URLs themselves: the verification key is now also written as a real file in the web root.

screenshots.caption: Dashboard - AI crawls, referral visits and engines seen over the last 30 days, which engines are reading you, and your average quotability score at install compared with now.
AI traffic trends - daily crawl volume across all engines, a per-engine trend chart for each crawler, and referral visits broken down by engine.
llms.txt tab - site name, summary and about text, with content sections and item counts selectable per language.
AI Traffic tab - tracking and retention settings with IP anonymisation, the daily activity chart, and the most-crawled URLs.
FAQ tab - bulk question and answer generation with FAQPage schema, plus per-item FAQ status across published content.
Readiness tab - every published item graded A to D, with analyse, FAQ and describe actions on each row.
